## Rule

**Marker-recolor (shape recolor).** Grid is **ALWAYS 7×7** (corpus-verified 200000/200000).
A shape of one color **C** sits in rows 1–5; a single **marker** cell of a different color
**M** sits at **(6,0)** — the unique nonzero in the last row and in column 0. Output = the
shape recolored to **M**, with the marker cell erased (→0). Rows 0 and 6 of the output are
all-zero.

Verified across all 264 embedded pairs (train 2 / test 1 / arc-gen 261) + 200k truth, 0
mismatches. M and C both span 1–9.

## Algorithm sketch

```
M = input[6,0]                      # marker color (bottom-left)
out = where(input != 0, M, 0)       # recolor every nonzero cell to M
out[6,0] = 0                        # erase the marker
```
Output one-hot [1,10,30,30]: ch0 = 1 at every non-shape cell of the 7×7 (incl the erased
marker), chM = shape cells (input foreground in rows 1–5), other channels 0, pad region
(rows/cols 7–29) all 0.

## Floor / open nibbles

No absolute floor claimed at 468 — strict shave on 525. **525→468 = the 5×5-box read**: the
ARC-GEN generator (`task_aabf363d.py`) builds the shape via `common.continuous_creature(_,5,5)`
in a **5×5 box**, then `+1`-shifts it into the 7×7 grid. So the shape ALWAYS lives in rows 1-5
**AND cols 1-5** — cols 0 and 6 (rows 1-5) are corpus-guaranteed background (verified 20k scan +
200k truth + ab byte-equal). The ch0 F32 read therefore shrinks to `bg7`=[1,1,5,5]=100 (−40), and
the bool/u8 mask planes to 25/25 (−10/−10). Prior task267.md notes only shrank the ROW span (7→5
rows) and called 5×7=140 "the F32-read floor" — they missed the symmetric COLUMN clip. The
remaining structure is forced:

- **bg7 F32 5×5 read = 100**: shape box is exactly rows 1-5 × cols 1-5 (5×5 = the generator's
  creature box). This IS the F32-read floor now (any tighter clip would drop a valid shape cell —
  the adversarial probe with a cell at every box corner confirms cols 1/5 and rows 1/5 are live).
  Any input read is F32 (Slice preserves dtype).
- **x2 2-channel carrier = 98**: mandated by the bias-leak law (#85.3) — a single channel
  cannot supply both ch0's all-ones constant and the shape mask; an in-conv bias to inject the
  `+1` paints the entire padded canvas (verified: ch0 lit on all 900 cells, pad-sum 851≠0).
- **active7 = 7×7**: ch0 (color 0) must be 1 at every non-shape cell INCLUDING rows 0 and 6
  and the erased marker, so the all-ones plane is structurally full-grid.
- Marker chain now omits color-0 marker read (`mk9` 36 vs `mk` 40), drops the `Sub(e0)` tensor,
  and uses `ConvInteger` to avoid six QLinearConv scalar params. The remaining marker tail is
  `mk9` 36 + two 9-byte cast/reshape tensors + 10-byte `w_sm`.

**FLOOR RE-VERIFIED 2026-06-24 (beta_p29 w9, bg7readshave angle)** — no sub-468 route; two
concrete empirical kills this session:
- **mask-chain reorder (Pad-bool-then-Cast) = 492 > 468.** Moving the Cast after the Pad makes the
  padded BOOL plane 7×7=49 instead of the 5×5 U8 cast at 25; net +24. The current order
  (Less→Cast at 5×5 [25]→Pad to 7×7 [49]) is the cheapest mask chain. The `bg7` F32 5×5 read (100)
  is the input-dtype floor (Slice preserves F32; single-channel 5×5 is the minimal shape surface —
  there is no U8 view of the F32 input, and Cast(input→U8) pays the full one-hot frame, traps §8g).
- **single-channel carrier (drop active7) = 291 but FUNCTIONALLY BROKEN.** Priced a 1-ch carrier
  (shape mask only, no all-ones plane): cost 291, but `ch0(0,0)=ch0(6,6)=0` on a synthetic probe —
  background cells outside the shape (incl rows 0/6 + erased marker) go dark, wrong. The `active7`
  full-7×7 all-ones plane is structurally mandatory and cannot be supplied via an in-conv bias
  (bias-leak law #85.3; ConvInteger has no bias, and a Conv-with-bias lights the pad region +
  reintroduces an F32 carrier). The 2-channel 7×7 U8 carrier (98) is forced, which in turn forces
  the `sm8` Pad to 7×7 (49) for the Concat dim-match. **468 stands as the family floor.**

**KILLED final-op families** (each > current 525, from the prior 826 floor work, still valid):
Equal-as-output ≥1100; Where-as-output(30×30) ≥1800 (e0 fills pad region — wrong); OneHot ≥900;
Concat ≫; arithmetic Mul/Add forces f32 carrier 1960. The integer-conv-as-output family (first
QLinearConv, now `ConvInteger`) is the winner here precisely because the weights are supplied as
a **runtime tensor** derived from the marker slice, so the conv is bilinear in the inputs — the
earlier "conv is linear" kill assumed fixed weights only.

## Don't-do log

- **"ALREADY OPTIMAL" (2026-05-20 note) was WRONG.** The old blend (1405) had full headroom;
  Where-routing cut 41% to 826. Do not trust "optimal" claims without a final-op kill table.
- **Don't use Equal+value-grid** (LIVE's way): the grader checks only `output>0`, so a clean
  integer value grid + Equal is wasted — it pays 4× f32 [1,1,7,7] planes. Route with **Where**.
- **Don't do the recolor in 30×30 / Where-at-output** — `1−ch0` is 1 in the pad region
  (off-grid reads as background-off), contaminating pad; and 30×30 intermediates (900) beat the
  490 carrier. Work in 7×7, **Pad last**.
- **QLinearConv-as-output IS the current best (584→546), via RUNTIME signed-INT8 weights.**
  The old "conv is linear, can't route bilinear" kill only applies to FIXED weights. Supplying
  the QLC weights as a runtime tensor (`marker_onehot − e0` from the marker slice) makes the
  conv bilinear in the inputs, so it routes shape→markercolor and does the 30×30 placement in
  one free output node. Do NOT rebuild the 826 Pad-last carrier.
- **Don't try an in-conv int32 BIAS to drop the active7 plane / 2nd carrier channel** — bias-leak
  law (#85.3): the free-output conv pads with all-channels-0, so a `+1` bias on ch0 lights the
  ENTIRE 30×30 (verified: pad-region ch0-sum 851≠0). Both the shape-mask plane and the all-ones
  complement-source must arrive as SEPARATE x channels. Pad-after-conv to confine it re-pays the
  490 carrier (854 total, worse).
- **Don't cast Where data to bool/int8/int16** — ORT rejects those (`Where(9)` no impl);
  uint8 is the only 1-byte valid Where-data dtype (ort_reality.md §2).
- **Don't widen the carrier to f32/F16** — uint8 (490) vs F16 (980) vs f32 (1960). The grader
  thresholds `>0`, so uint8 0/1 is sufficient; output dtype uint8 is fine (ab byte-equal to
  LIVE's bool confirmed).
